name: mina
title: Mina
description: Socket level networking using TCP or UDP with Apache Mina 2.x.
label: networking

properties.name: protocol
properties.description: Protocol to use

properties.name: host
properties.description: Hostname to use. Use localhost or 0.0.0.0 for local server as consumer. For producer use the hostname or ip address of the remote server.

properties.name: port
properties.description: Port number

properties.name: disconnect
properties.description: Whether to disconnect(close) from Mina session right after use. Can be used for both consumer and producer.

properties.name: minaLogger
properties.description: You can enable the Apache MINA logging filter. Apache MINA uses slf4j logging at INFO level to log all input and output.

properties.name: sync
properties.description: Setting to set endpoint as one-way or request-response.

properties.name: timeout
properties.description: You can configure the timeout that specifies how long to wait for a response from a remote server. The timeout unit is in milliseconds, so 60000 is 60 seconds.

properties.name: writeTimeout
properties.description: Maximum amount of time it should take to send data to the MINA session. Default is 10000 milliseconds.

properties.name: clientMode
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: If the clientMode is true, mina consumer will connect the address as a TCP client.

properties.name: muteException
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: If enabled and an Exchange failed processing on the consumer side the response written back to the remote peer won't contain the exception's class, message or stack trace.

properties.name: bridgeErrorHandler
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

properties.name: exceptionHandler
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: To let the consumer use a custom ExceptionHandler. Notice if the option bridgeErrorHandler is enabled then this option is not in use. By default the consumer will deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

properties.name: exchangePattern
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: Sets the exchange pattern when the consumer creates an exchange.

properties.name: noReplyLogLevel
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: If sync is enabled this option dictates MinaConsumer which logging level to use when logging a there is no reply to send back.

properties.name: cachedAddress
properties.label: producer,advanced
properties.description: Whether to create the InetAddress once and reuse. Setting this to false allows to pickup DNS changes in the network.

properties.name: lazySessionCreation
properties.label: producer,advanced
properties.description: Sessions can be lazily created to avoid exceptions, if the remote server is not up and running when the Camel producer is started.

properties.name: lazyStartProducer
properties.label: producer,advanced
properties.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

properties.name: disconnectOnNoReply
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: If sync is enabled then this option dictates MinaConsumer if it should disconnect where there is no reply to send back.

properties.name: maximumPoolSize
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Number of worker threads in the worker pool for TCP and UDP

properties.name: orderedThreadPoolExecutor
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Whether to use ordered thread pool, to ensure events are processed orderly on the same channel.

properties.name: transferExchange
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Only used for TCP. You can transfer the exchange over the wire instead of just the body. The following fields are transferred: In body, Out body, fault body, In headers, Out headers, fault headers, exchange properties, exchange exception. This requires that the objects are serializable. Camel will exclude any non-serializable objects and log it at WARN level. Also make sure to configure objectCodecPattern to (star) to allow transferring java objects.

properties.name: allowDefaultCodec
properties.label: codec
properties.description: The mina component installs a default codec if both, codec is null and textline is false. Setting allowDefaultCodec to false prevents the mina component from installing a default codec as the first element in the filter chain. This is useful in scenarios where another filter must be the first in the filter chain, like the SSL filter.

properties.name: codec
properties.label: codec
properties.description: To use a custom minda codec implementation.

properties.name: decoderMaxLineLength
properties.label: codec
properties.description: To set the textline protocol decoder max line length. By default the default value of Mina itself is used which are 1024.

properties.name: encoderMaxLineLength
properties.label: codec
properties.description: To set the textline protocol encoder max line length. By default the default value of Mina itself is used which are Integer.MAX_VALUE.

properties.name: encoding
properties.label: codec
properties.description: You can configure the encoding (a charset name) to use for the TCP textline codec and the UDP protocol. If not provided, Camel will use the JVM default Charset

properties.name: filters
properties.label: codec
properties.description: You can set a list of Mina IoFilters to use.

properties.name: objectCodecPattern
properties.label: codec
properties.description: Accept the wildcard specified classes for Object deserialization, unless they are otherwise rejected. Multiple patterns can be separated by comma.

properties.name: textline
properties.label: codec
properties.description: Only used for TCP. If no codec is specified, you can use this flag to indicate a text line based codec; if not specified or the value is false, then Object Serialization is assumed over TCP.

properties.name: textlineDelimiter
properties.label: codec
properties.description: Only used for TCP and if textline=true. Sets the text line delimiter to use. If none provided, Camel will use DEFAULT. This delimiter is used to mark the end of text.

properties.name: hostnameVerification
properties.label: security
properties.description: Whether to check that the certificate of the server matches the host Camel connects to, when SSL is used by the producer, or by the consumer in client mode. When disabled, any certificate accepted by the trust store is accepted, whatever host it was issued for.

properties.name: sslContextParameters
properties.label: security
properties.description: To configure SSL security.
